import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss
import os

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Load data
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")

# Extract feature columns (excluding id and species)
feature_cols = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in ["id", "species"]]
X = train_df[feature_cols].values
y = train_df["species"].values
X_test = test_df[feature_cols].values

# Encode target labels
le = LabelEncoder()
y_encoded = le.fit_transform(y)
species_names = le.classes_

# Split for validation (stratified to preserve species distribution)
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    X, y_encoded, test_size=0.2, stratify=y_encoded, random_state=42
)

# Train random forest classifier with calibration
base_clf = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=500,
    max_depth=15,
    min_samples_split=5,
    min_samples_leaf=2,
    class_weight="balanced",
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,
)

# Use isotonic calibration for better probability estimates
calibrated_clf = CalibratedClassifierCV(base_clf, method="isotonic", cv=5)
calibrated_clf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Validate on hold-out set
val_probs = calibrated_clf.predict_proba(X_val)
val_loss = log_loss(y_val, val_probs)
print(f"Validation LogLoss: {val_loss:.6f}")

# Train final model on full training data
calibrated_clf.fit(X, y_encoded)

# Predict on test set
test_probs = calibrated_clf.predict_proba(X_test)

# Ensure probabilities are in valid range [1e-15, 1-1e-15]
test_probs = np.clip(test_probs, 1e-15, 1 - 1e-15)

# Normalize rows to sum to 1 (as per competition instructions, though not strictly needed)
test_probs = test_probs / test_probs.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

# Create submission DataFrame
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(test_probs, columns=species_names)
submission_df.insert(0, "id", test_df["id"])

# Save submission
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print("Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
